title: Characterization of Cellular Communication During Perineural Invasion of Head and Neck Tumors
summary:
The goal of this research project is to investigate molecular changes and their significance for tumor-nerve interactions using human tumor samples from patients with head and neck carcinomas. For this purpose, only existing tumor samples obtained as part of routine clinical care will be used. Staining of the tissue sections will be used to examine the expression and spatial distribution of selected markers in the tumor microenvironment. In particular, the study will investigate in which cell types the markers are detectable and whether their expression or spatial distribution is associated with evidence of nerve invasion.
For the study, patients with known nerve invasion status will be enrolled and divided into groups with and without this invasion. The experimentally collected data will then be compared with existing routine clinical-pathological data, including tumor stage, lymph node status, response to therapy, recurrence, and survival. In addition, staining techniques will be used to investigate the spatial co-expression of selected markers with relevant cell types and neural structures.
conditions: Malignant neoplasms of lip, oral cavity and pharynx

interventions.name: Retrospectively, tumor patients treated at Heidelberg University Hospital from January 1, 2012, through September 30, 2026, for whom PNI status is available, will be divided into two groups. The main group consists of patients with nerve invasion. The control group consists of patients without nerve
